structure.title: Prologue and parodos · A city asks its saviour for help
structure.text: Petitioners gather outside the palace. Oedipus once solved the Sphinx's riddle. Faced with plague, he promises to identify the murderer of the previous king, publicly laying down terms that he must subsequently honour.

structure.title: First episode – fourth stasimon · Witnesses who would rather keep quiet
structure.text: A prophet, a queen, a messenger and a shepherd each know portions of the past. Someone trying to put Oedipus at ease can give him exactly the detail that makes further inquiry unavoidable.

people.name: Oedipus
people.text: His eagerness to answer in person has won him trust. He has also grown accustomed to treating reluctance as resistance, even when he badly needs the reluctant person's testimony.

people.name: Jocasta
people.role: Queen and witness to an earlier reign
people.text: She has reasons grounded in experience for distrusting predictions. Her attempt to show how one prophecy failed requires her to describe an old journey in unusual detail.

people.name: Tiresias
people.role: The seer summoned as a witness
people.text: Thebes calls for a man believed to have access to knowledge others lack. When that man would prefer to keep silent, Oedipus treats his reluctance as a betrayal of the city. The interview places a frightening condition on a ruler who wants to hear the truth. He may have to let someone speak to him as no subject ordinarily dares.

context.title: Pollution and responsibility
context.text: The oracle connects a public calamity to an unpunished killing. The hunt for a culprit consequently concerns people who were nowhere near the crime. The citizens need an answer even if their king would be better off without one.

notice.text: Keep track of who actually saw the attack.
notice.why: Numbers, roads and hearsay carry more weight than a general resemblance between stories. Oedipus pursues the case with the stubbornness that once made him a successful solver of riddles.

notice.text: Hear the older meaning of each promise when it comes back.
notice.why: What sounds generous when a king volunteers to suffer alongside his city may sound altogether different once the speaker knows more. The wording can stay exactly the same.

opening: Thebes is dying of plague, and Oedipus intends to save it. He has solved a deadly riddle before; now he must find the murderer whose unpunished crime is poisoning the city. Witnesses resist, warnings accumulate, and the king grows furious at anyone withholding information. Sophocles makes the investigation terrifying because Oedipus' determination is so understandable. He takes responsibility, demands evidence, and refuses convenient silence, bringing the full force of his intelligence to a discovery that others would prefer him never to make.
